THE ‘JANSEN’ STRADIVARI VIOLONCELLO AN IMPORTANT VIOLONCELLO, by Antonius Stradivarius, Cremona 1721, labelled Antonius Stradivarius Cremononfis Faciebat Anno 1721, the handsome two-piece back of wood of irregular narrow curl, sloping upwards from the joint, the ribs and the head of similar wood of faint curl, the table of pine of medium to broad grain in centre, the varnish of a rich orange-brown colour, length of back 29 7/16in. (747mm.), in a portable travelling case (2) Certificates: Max Möller, Amsterdam, 29th July 1949; Hamma & Co., Stuttgart, 12th September 1953 Literature: Goodkind, Herbert K. Violin Iconography of Antonio Stradivari, ill. pp. 541; The Strad, Lewin (Robert) Vol. 86, No. 1027, November 1975 Provenance: Samuel Brill; Jacques Français; Claus Frank; Hamma & Co.; Jansen; David Laurie; Max Möller; Van Leemren Boomka; See Goodkind pp. 725   From the researches of Robert Lewin it would seem most likely that the ‘Jansen’ from whom this violoncello takes its name was the friend of David Laurie referred to in his book The Reminiscences of a Fiddle Dealer. This gentleman was an amateur cellist and a collector. He was a friend of Vuillaume and Vieuxtemps. On his death his collection passed to David Laurie. Of the later owners of this Violoncello, Van Leemren Boomka was solo cellist with the Amsterdam Concertgebouw and Samuel Brill was his successor in this position. (See COLOUR ILLUSTRATION)
